Subject: Initial RFP questions — pilot tranche & per-token math

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — Stratos Tech is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Procurement looped me in with a few pricing questions as we scope a Q3 pilot. Attached is our short RFP and expected pilot volume profile (monthly token curve). Two quick asks:  

1) We want to understand the difference in economics between a marginal-breakpoint ladder (pay the lower marginal rate for usage within each band) vs a blended rate (single effective $/k tokens across total consumption). Can you provide a one-page worked example using the attached pilot volumes?

2) For pilots, we prefer a tranche-based commit (90-day pilot with a small committed token bucket and the option to true-up into a larger annual commit). Is Redwood willing to do a provisional tranche/phase with a smaller upfront commit and a pre-agreed rate schedule if we convert?

Procurement has the RFP and the team (procurement@stratos.tech) will join future threads. Can you loop in the right commercial contacts and share a short worked example?

Attachments: Stratos_RFP_Q3.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Thanks,
Anna Li

Stratos Tech

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Initial RFP questions — pilot tranche & per-token math

Hi Anna — great to hear from you and glad the demo landed. Looping Ben and Marissa for commercial sign-off on provisional tranche language.

Below is a concise worked example and our standard position. I'll attach a simple MAP (pilot-MAP-v1.xlsx) after we agree on structure.

Worked example (illustrative):
- Pilot period expected consumption: 3 months = 75M tokens total (month1 10M / month2 25M / month3 40M).
- Proposed ladder (marginal):
  * 0–20M tokens: $0.008 / 1k tokens
  * 20–60M tokens: $0.006 / 1k tokens
  * 60M+ tokens: $0.004 / 1k tokens
- Marginal math: first 20M at 0.008 = $160; next 40M at 0.006 = $240; final 15M at 0.004 = $60; total = $460 => effective blended $/1k = $460 / 75M * 1000 = $0.00613 / 1k tokens.
- Blended offer (single rate): If we offered a single blended rate to hit same total $460 across 75M tokens it would be $0.00613 / 1k — but blended offers remove the visible volume incentives and can be harder to reconcile in true-ups.

Our standard commercial points for tranche pilots:
- Provisional tranche: small committed bucket for pilot (e.g., 50M tokens) with pre-agreed ladder breakpoints if customer converts to annual.
- True-up: if customer converts within 90 days, committed tokens roll into annual commit and margins are reconciled to the annual ladder; credits applied for over/under usage per agreed rules.
- Clawbacks/credits: we typically avoid retroactive credits beyond a 120-day window and recommend a capped true-up credit to keep accounting clean.

Ben/Marissa — is the above within the range we can approve for a pilot with Stratos? If so I can generate the MAP and sample DocuSign clause.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial RFP questions — pilot tranche & per-token math

Rishi / Anna — thanks for the context. A couple of commercial adjustments I propose so this pilot is both low-friction for Stratos and preserves predictable economics for us:

1) Pilot commit suggestion: 50M committed tokens for 90 days, with a stage gate at conversion: if Stratos converts within 90 days, the 50M applies as a credit against the first quarter of the annual commit.
2) Ladder tweak (to keep upside protection): 0–20M $0.008 | 20–80M $0.0055 | 80M+ $0.0040 — this gives stronger incentive to scale through the pilot while keeping a margin buffer.
3) Marginal vs blended: offer both in the MAP but list marginal as default; blended can be offered as an optional simplified billing model for procurement but with a small admin premium (+5%) to account for reconciliation complexity.

Anna — if procurement needs a single line-item (blended) we can provide it, but we prefer marginal-tier billing for long-term renewals.

I'll approve a one-time pilot discount of 7.5% on the marginal bands for this customer (exec sign-off pending) if procurement signs the MAP within two weeks.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Global Sales
Redwood Inference

- MAP workbook: month-by-month true-up worksheet, scenario tabs (expected / high / low). Includes sample invoices showing marginal vs blended outcomes and shows the 7.5% pilot discount applied to marginal bands.
- Draft pilot clause (paragraph): "Customer and Redwood agree to a 90-day provisional pilot commit of 50,000,000 tokens.
